title: Letters From You and Your Name

lessons.title: ங (ṅa) — the nasal before the க in நீங்கள்
lessons.gloss: the single character ங — the nasal before the க in நீங்கள்

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ங and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: read ◌ை and ஸ aloud, and write each once.
Now say நீங்கள் (nīṅgaḷ), "you (respectful)". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.
ங — ṅa.

It is the nasal in the middle of நீங்கள் (nīṅgaḷ), the respectful "you". Say nīṅgaḷ slowly: the ṅ is made at the back of the mouth, where k is made, which is why ங (ṅa) nearly always stands right before க.
1. start here: draw the detached upright down, then lift.
2. put the pen down again and climb the tall left body.
3. without lifting, carry the top bar right and return inward.
4. without lifting, descend into the rounded inner turn.
5. without lifting, carry the low bar to the right.
6. without lifting, return left and finish up the inner stem — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 1.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order, not a national standard — Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation. Source: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 2, ங (ṅa) (University of Texas at Austin), p. 191.

[YOU WRITE: ஸ, then ங, from memory]

segments.text: Which character is this — ங? (ṅa.) Which word did it come from? (நீங்கள், nīṅgaḷ, "you (respectful)".)

lessons.title: ள (ḷa) — the l at the end of நீங்கள்
lessons.gloss: the single character ள — the l at the end of நீங்கள்

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ள and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: read ஸ and ங (ṅa) aloud, and write each once.
Now say நீங்கள் (nīṅgaḷ), "you (respectful)". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.
ள — ḷa.

It closes நீங்கள் (nīṅgaḷ). This is the Tamil l made with the tongue curled back. You already write ல (la) and ழ (ḻa); ள (ḷa) is the third l, and the dot under the romanization (ḷ) is how the book tells them apart.
1. start here: curl around the large left loop.
2. without lifting, turn inward through the loop.
3. without lifting, descend around the inner curl, then lift.
4. put the pen down again and rise on the adjoining upright.
5. without lifting, carry the top bar right, then lift.
6. put the pen down again and descend the separate right upright — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 2.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order, not a national standard — Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation. Source: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 12, ள (ḷa) (University of Texas at Austin), p. 195.

lessons.title: ◌ீ (ī) — the long i on நீ
lessons.gloss: the single character ◌ீ — the long i on நீ

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: ◌ீ and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: read ங (ṅa) and ள (ḷa) aloud, and write each once.
Now say நீ (nī), "you (familiar)". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.
It is the sign on நீ (nī), "you". You already write its short partner ◌ி (i), the hook from நன்றி. The long sign ◌ீ ends in a curl instead of an open hook. One curl more, one beat longer.
Put your pen on ◌ீ (ī) and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

This book does not yet tell you where to start the character or which way to travel. That is a real thing, taught with real variation from school to school, and it is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.

lessons.title: ◌ெ — the short e in பெயர்
lessons.gloss: the single character ◌ெ — the short e in பெயர்

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page

segments.text: Before the new one: read ள (ḷa) and ◌ீ (ī) aloud, and write each once.
Now say பெயர் (peyar), "name". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one character out of it and puts it in your hand.

It is the sign on the first syllable of பெயர் (peyar), "name". Like ◌ை, it is written on the left of its consonant and sounded after it. You already know its long partner ◌ே (ē) from பேசு. Put the two side by side and compare the shapes: that difference is the difference between pe and pē.
Put your pen on ◌ெ and follow its line. Copy the shape you can see — slowly, and larger than it is printed.

This book does not yet tell you where to start the character or which way to travel. That is a real thing, taught with real variation from school to school, and it is not written down here until it can be written down with a source. Copying what is in front of you needs no such source, and it is how the shape gets into your hand in the meantime.
